routes.label: Prove necessity and construct a shared diagonal

answerCheck.reason: With fourth rod length t, choose a diagonal d satisfying 4<d<10 and |15-t|<d<15+t. The intervals overlap exactly for 5<t<25. Any such d forms two nondegenerate triangles, which can be glued on opposite sides to make a simple positive-area quadrilateral. Integers 6 through 24 give 19 rods, but 7 and 15 are already used, leaving 17, B. The existing four-side feasibility scope explicitly includes necessity and diagonal-based sufficiency; reuse it with interval support rather than create another quadrilateral scope or pretend triangle feasibility states the four-side criterion.

The two nondegenerate triangles require 4<d<10 and |15-x|<d<15+x. These intervals overlap exactly when |15-x|<10, or 5<x<25. There are 19 integer lengths from 6 through 24; removing the already-used lengths 7 and 15 leaves 17.
Any side x is shorter than the other three combined, so x<26-x and integer x<=12. An isosceles trapezoid with bases 12 and 4 and legs 5 has height 3 and perimeter 26, attaining 12.

Each side must be at most 15. The number of ordered positive tuples summing to 32 is C(31,3)-4C(16,3)=2255. Exactly 15 have the form (a,b,a,b), where a+b=16; one of these is (8,8,8,8). Thus the cyclic-shift orbits number (2255-15)/4+(15-1)/2+1=568. Reflections are not additionally identified.
